source_record.english: "Suppose," one may begin, "that a person takes a weapon and delivers a blow to someone else which is sure to kill him, but then this murderer himself happens to die, either before his victim or together with him--at the same time. Can we say then that the actual "commission" stage of a full path of action has occurred for such a murderer, or not?"

proposed_errata.expected: For human review: 'CHI NGES PA'I MTSON BSNUN NAS is the supported weapon-striking candidate. No automatic source replacement.
proposed_errata.evidence: ACIP344 and its physical ASCII read MTSAN; wylie mtshan is faithful. Complete mtshan records support name/sign/night and do not list weapon; mtshon records explicitly have weapon, and a complete mtshon bsnun scaffold has the Sanskrit weapon-struck sense but no HGM equivalent. The local English explicitly says takes a weapon and delivers a blow. Ten full mtshon bsnun corpus records were read: C05:459/460, C11:140, C12:110, C16:969/970, C18:247, GK:192/363/364. Different-context C11:140 explicitly pairs the construction with struck them with a weapon; C05:459 and C12:110 likewise concern weapon strikes. They support usage, not a corrected witness to this exact sentence; C05:459/460 also have their own field-boundary distribution and are not treated as clean word pairs. Counterevidence: C16:865 repeats all three344 fields exactly, including MTSAN. The same MTSAN BSNUN also occurs metaphorically at C05:462/C16:972, struck a blow to the reality body. That repeated source form makes an isolated local corruption unproved and leaves nonstandard/variant wording possible. Four exact mtshan bsnun rows and ten mtshon bsnun rows were measured; no direct344/MTSAN BSNUN register match among200 records. Full fields are below1500 and physically complete. Propose LOW/PROBABLE spelling review, not CONFIRMED and not an ingest/converter correction. Preserve mtshan unbanked and source/master unchanged.
